sectorSummary.overview: Gold-led AUM growth and operating leverage supported higher profits across the five calls. Rising overdue classifications under new repayment formats, stronger competition and funding-cost pressure make collections and disciplined pricing central to the H2 outlook.

trends.text: Gold loans continued to drive strong balance-sheet growth and remained the largest business or a major growth engine.
Scale and operating leverage supported stronger quarterly profitability, although asset-quality indicators were mixed.

tailwinds.text: Branch expansion and existing distribution capacity support customer acquisition and further gold-loan growth.
Co-lending and assignment partnerships provide capacity to grow while managing balance-sheet capital.

headwinds.text: Managements linked higher gold overdues to customers adapting to shorter-tenure or periodic servicing products; collateral protection does not remove collection and provisioning work.
Higher market rates and bank borrowing resets could increase funding costs, requiring pricing, funding-mix or efficiency responses.

opportunities.text: Capri is scaling smaller-ticket gold lending alongside housing, MSME and construction finance, with a ₹65,000 Cr FY28 AUM target.
IIFL expects housing disbursement momentum and affordable-housing distribution investment to support 18–20% FY27 home-finance AUM growth.

risks.text: Muthoot Finance and Manappuram gave no firm quarter-end level for gold Stage 2 normalization.
IIFL’s proposed equity raise creates dilution and near-term return uncertainty; Manappuram also faces elevated vehicle-finance NPAs.

insights.text: Capri retained ₹50,000 Cr FY27 AUM guidance and now indicates about ₹1,600 Cr PAT; its shorter-tenure schemes were withdrawn after delinquency spikes.
Muthoot Finance’s FY27 AUM-growth outlook is about 25%, versus its 15% starting-year view.
